headline: A heavy data morning — PCE and GDP set the tone as chips wobble and oil slides.
stance: Markets sit near flat into a packed 8:30am ET data slate — PCE, GDP, durable goods and jobless claims — that is today's pivot: a soft print revives rate-cut hopes, a hot one reinforces higher-for-longer and pressures tech. Tech stress is concentrated in chips (Nasdaq vol gauge 30 vs VIX 18.6); credit and funding stay calm. The engine holds Risk On · Neutral.

news.head: Oil dropped sharply Wednesday
news.body: Brent crude −4.3% to $73.18 and WTI −3.9% to $69.87 (prior close) on reports of Iran diplomatic progress. Gold eased to ~$3,998 pre-market (prior close ~$4,016).

news.head: Heavy 8:30am data slate
news.body: May PCE inflation, the Q1 GDP final revision (consensus 1.6%, down from 2.0% initial), May durable goods orders, and weekly jobless claims all land at 8:30am ET.

news.head: Germany confidence turns positive
news.body: Germany's economic confidence index turned positive for the first time since the Middle East war began — an early sign European sentiment is stabilizing.

news.head: Bank of England on hold
news.body: The BoE held rates at 3.75% — no change.

implications: PCE and GDP at 8:30am are today's pivot: a soft reading revives rate-cut expectations and could lift equities; a beat reinforces higher-for-longer pressure, especially on tech and growth.
Oil's drop eases inflation pressure (bond-supportive) but sustained weakness signals demand concern and weighs on energy earnings.
The yen at multi-year extremes is the sleeper risk — a rapid reversal from current levels could trigger global capital repatriation and broad equity pressure.
Positioning: Copper speculators are the most crowded in 3 years — a contrarian warning; don't chase industrial metals here.

watch.head: 8:30am ET data
watch.body: PCE, GDP final revision, durable goods, jobless claims.

watch.head: Gold above $4,000
watch.body: holding above $4,000 is a key sentiment level.

watch.head: USD/JPY toward 160
watch.body: any move from 161.75 toward 160 signals yen carry unwinding has begun.

watch.head: Chip stocks
watch.body: watch whether Asia's overnight selling pressure extends through the US open.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
sections.prose: The 10-year Treasury yield closed Wednesday at 4.41%, the 2-year at 4.11% — the curve barely positive at +30bp and still historically flat; inflation-adjusted yields at 2.23% remain restrictive. USD/JPY at 161.75 (prior close) leaves the yen at a 3-year extreme after the Bank of Japan raised rates to 1.0% on June 16. 10-year inflation expectations are anchored at 2.18%.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no rate-cut bets left — a contrarian floor; a soft PCE print could quickly lift short-term Treasuries.

sections.title: Equity Markets
sections.prose: The S&P 500 closed Wednesday at 7,358 (−0.1%), the Nasdaq −0.43%, the Dow +0.35%; futures point to a near-flat open. Tech is under pressure — memory-chip names fell sharply in Asia and the weakness extended to Nvidia and Apple; the Nasdaq vol gauge sits at 30 vs VIX 18.6, with stress concentrated in growth. About 62% of the S&P trades above its 50-day average — breadth narrowing.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left on small caps — a contrarian floor; small caps could outperform if today's data surprises soft.

single_name.note: (Matador Resources, an oil & gas producer) — insiders buying plus quiet institutional block accumulation; a way to play energy if oil finds a floor.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
sections.prose: Investment-grade spreads are 74bp and high-yield 271bp over investment grade — both in normal range, no stress. Financial conditions stay loose and bank reserves are robust at $3 trillion. The quiet vulnerability: primary dealers hold near-record high-yield inventories, leaving limited room to absorb a sudden wave of client selling if sentiment shifts.
